volume_note: volume load = sets x reps x kg; an index comparable only against itself

entries.note: FIRST LOADED calf session — single leg with a dumbbell, 3 s up / 3 s down. Prescribed 3x8; he took the LAST set to 12 reps each leg and that brought the burn, so the load is correctly placed for roughly 8-12. LOAD NOT STATED (prescribed 8-10 kg) — ask, it is the number the whole progression hangs on
LOAD CONFIRMED 10 kg (operator-stated), supersedes the 'not stated' row above. Single leg + 10 kg dumbbell = ~81 kg through one calf at 71 kg bodyweight. Burn arrived at 12 reps on the last set

Last set 12 reps. LIMITED BY THE THIGH, not the calf — holding ~30 deg knee flexion under load makes it a partial isometric squat, and he has quad DOMS today. FIX: move the soleus work to a SEATED calf raise, where the thigh is supported and the load sits on the knee, so the quad stops being the limiter. Also: hint of the right-calf niggle again in the bent-knee position

SUBSTITUTE for band inversion — band could not be found. Isometric, foot pressed inward against the opposite foot, 5 s holds, both sides. Weaker stimulus than the band; restore the band or use a cable column next session
both sides, progressed from 2x30 s on 9 Sep. No leg raise yet — time added before complexity
SINGLE LEG, bodyweight, both legs. Prescribed 3 sets; felt easy. Roughly double the per-calf load of the 8 Sep double-leg version
SINGLE LEG, bodyweight, both legs. Prescribed 2 sets, did 3 because it felt easy. Next rung is EXTERNAL LOAD (dumbbell in hand or seated calf raise), gated on the 11 Sep morning response
'fairly easy' — moved from 'not easy, not at failure' at the same 16 kg on 8 Sep. RAISE to 18 kg next session
'hard at the end' — third session at 10 kg, and a shade easier than the 'at limit' of 28 Aug and 8 Sep. Hold 10 kg, add a third set before adding weight

RETEST CONFIRMED THE HYPOTHESIS: with the prescribed 45-60 s rest, 30 kg went from '3rd set near limit' (8 Sep, ~15 s rest) to 'suitable or slightly easy' at MORE reps (3x10 vs 3x9). The 8 Sep near-limit reading was a rest artefact, not the load. RAISE next session. Load 30 kg and the rest actually taken both ASSUMED — not restated by him today

'suitably hard at end' — same verdict as 8 Sep at the same 35 kg, so this one is correctly placed and has NOT drifted easy the way chest press and lat pulldown have. Hold 35 kg. Load still ASSUMED, never stated

'on the easy side' at 16 kg, up from 10 kg — the +6 kg was absorbed without comment, and this is the first session it was loaded for the LEGS rather than held back for the calf. RAISE again next session (20-24 kg) and add a third set
'get hard towards the end' — third session at 2x45 s and still a genuine effort, unlike almost everything else this session. Hold 2x45 s
both sides, post-easy-run filler; the rest of the offered hip/core block and the stretches were not done. Deliberately calf-sparing — single-leg heel-raise progression held for 10 Sep
original warm-up as first written
original warm-up version, done before the cut; bodyweight, no pause
soleus-biased, bodyweight, wall-ladder rung, heels to horizontal only; 15 reps FAIRLY EASY, no burn. Disliked the arm strain of bracing on the bars — switch to a mat/step edge next time
gastroc, bodyweight, edge of gym mat; 15 reps fairly easy, slight burn on the last reps of the final two sets only. Mat edge preferred over the wall ladder
tib post, both legs; done as part of block 2, no detail given
done both legs; operator judged it pointless. L/R difference not reported — candidate for cutting from the programme
CONFIRMED 16 kg on dumbbells (supersedes the 28 Aug ASSUMED figure). Not easy, but no burn and not at failure — 16 kg is a genuine working weight, roughly 2-3 reps in reserve
still AT LIMIT at 10 kg, second session running — hold 10 kg again next time, no progression. Taken out of prescribed order to keep the bench
'felt appropriately hard' — the +5 kg step was right, hold 35 kg next session. LOAD STILL ASSUMED from prescription: operator did not state the pin position
'too easy' — second session running at 10 kg, held deliberately for the calf, not for the legs. RAISE next session (16 kg or nearest) provided the calf stayed quiet through these
first two sets too easy, third near limit — 30 kg is correctly placed for a 3-set session. Hold 30 kg and build reps toward 3x12 before adding weight. LOAD STILL ASSUMED: pin position not stated
'suitably hard' — same as 28 Aug at limit; hold 2x45 s again next session
at limit
felt easy but not ineffective; pattern rehearsal on fatigued legs
easy — load too light, raise next time
near limit; this is the working weight, hold it
corrective set to find baseline; load ASSUMED from prescription, not stated
moderately easy — raise next time; load ASSUMED from prescription, not stated
moderately hard — hold this weight next session; load ASSUMED from prescription, not stated
